collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The village wants the researchers to study its own problems: let villagers choose, or let researchers choose.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The researchers have spent a year studying the color of the sunset. (friend) and the other children have drawn a picture of the village they want, with safe paths and a well that does not run dry, and have given it to (subject), a researcher. Maybe the village should decide what gets studied. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) asks the gathering what problems most need solving. The answer is the well. The researchers study the well for a season, and find a better place to dig. (friend) says (friend.his/her) picture was right.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) keeps studying sunsets. The village is unimpressed. But one evening, the sunset shows a storm coming two days early, and everyone is very glad of the researchers. (subject) then studies the well anyway.
